title: Stretch, smudge, and three tanks of sodium
learning_goal: See a dynamo as a race between stretching and smudging measured by Rm, understand why liquid-sodium dynamos are hard and turbulent, and meet the three that worked, including VKS, which flips.
takeaway: A flow amplifies a field when stretching beats smudging; only three sodium experiments got there, and one of them, VKS, flips like the Earth.
notes: Every scene is ready (no simulation, D4); every fact is on the site (report, thesis plan, prep module 3, supervisors page), so all claim-bearing scenes carry the CONTEXT badge; the only external citations are the seafloor ages reused from 00.3. The chapter card (T4) sits in the 3.4-s lead-in of 02.1 (no staircase: it is planted in 03.7). Changes against the outline, to review: (1) 02.5 gains an unnumbered predict beat ('Should it matter what metal the discs are made of?', hold 2.5 s): the pacing grammar asks 1-2 per chapter and ch02 had none; Q1-Q8 keep their numbers. (2) 02.3 names Pm in the narration (the question card needs it) and draws the Re dial green, not blue (Re is a control parameter in the colour key). (3) 02.1 says 'in a perfect conductor, field lines would be threads frozen into the fluid' (frozen flux holds only as eta goes to zero, P3:214, P3:305). (4) The VKS numbers sit on a separate lab card and on the formula layer, never on the qualitative curve (C6, F5). Words budgeted at 125-130 effective words per minute of target; estimates use the assembler formula (146 raw words per minute, 0.9 s per paragraph break, holds, lead-in and tail). Lexicon pins wanted: Cadarache, Karlsruhe, Prandtl (audio/lexicon.json; Rm, Pm, VKS, DRESDYN are already pinned). Adversarial review 2026-11-08: changes and evidence in script/_review/ch02.md.

scenes.title: Frozen threads

params.note: schematic tuning values (pixels, scene seconds), not physical data; the two panels differ only by kappa

sentences.text: What kind of motion can grow a {b}magnetic field{/}?
In a perfect conductor, field lines would be threads frozen into the fluid.
Wherever the {u}flow{/} stretches a thread, the field along it grows stronger.
Real metals let the threads smudge, like spreading ink.
The smudging speed is set by the metal's {param}magnetic diffusivity{/}.
Same flow, two metals.
A good conductor smudges slowly: the threads stay sharp.
A poor one smudges fast: the threads blur away.

onscreen.title: Stretch, smudge, and three tanks of sodium

scenes.visual: Render class dense2d (Canvas 2D; Kit.twoInks, motif M3 two inks). Starting point: scenes/_prototype/a_fieldlines.html, which already integrates a cellular flow and a frozen material line with Scene.stepper (fixed step, identical frames whatever the seek order). LEAD-IN (3.4 s, no voice): Kit.chapterCard(ctx, {num: '02', title: onscreen.title, level: 'L1', levelFrom: 'L1', at: 0.2, out: 'motion-0.3'}) with no tier, so no staircase is drawn (the staircase M7 is planted in 03.7, E1); the rail (left gutter) shows L1 for 3 s; whoosh at 0.2 (sfx). On 'motion-0.3': the card's faint vermillion dipole lines thin out and the whole frame becomes the two-inks field: a blue (--u) cellular flow of params.cells = 4 x 2 cells drawn as faint aligned blue segments, params.tracers blue tracer particles with short trails, and ONE horizontal vermillion (--b) material line across the frame at params.line_y_frac of the height. On 'threads': the line starts to be carried by the flow with no diffusion at all (the ideal, perfect-conductor limit); the reference lower-third 'Reference' / 'Alfvén 1942 · frozen flux' for 4 s. On 'stretch': the line is stretched and folded around the cells; each segment's brightness follows its local stretch factor (log scale, clipped at params.stretch_clip), so the longest folds glow brightest; label 'stretching' and a chalk pen arrow (M9) along the brightest fold. On 'smudge': diffusion switches on: the line becomes a Gaussian ribbon whose width grows like the square root of 2 x kappa x (t - t_smudge) and whose peak brightness falls as it spreads (kappa = params.kappa_px2_s.small for now); a light grey halo grows around it; label 'diffusion' in grey. On 'diffusivity': the green (--param) label 'magnetic diffusivity' appears under 'diffusion' (the word only: the symbol eta waits for 02.2). On 'split': T1 split in 1.2 s: the frame divides into two panels of about 860 x 620 px side by side (40 px gutter), both running the SAME flow from the SAME initial line (same seed, same stepper), so the panels differ only by kappa; green labels above them, 'small diffusivity' (left) and 'large diffusivity' (right), with 'good conductor' and 'poor conductor' under them in --fg-2. On 'sharp': left panel, kappa = params.kappa_px2_s.small: the thread stays a few pixels wide, folds sharp and bright; tag 'stretching wins'. On 'blur': right panel, kappa = params.kappa_px2_s.large: the ribbon swells into a diffuse haze whose colour fades from vermillion toward the grey of the halo as its peak drops below 30 % (the grey blur wins); tag 'diffusion wins'. Tracers keep drifting in both panels to the end (idle motion; never 3 s of stillness). No viscosity, honey or water metaphor (critique_accuracy B5): the only difference between the panels is the magnetic diffusivity. Chip SCHEMATIC (grey dashed) from 'motion', bottom-right of the stage, above y 880. Badge CONTEXT top-right from 'motion'. Key colours: blue, vermillion, green (three). Look reference for field lines wound and expelled by eddies: prep/p3-mhd-dynamo/figures/expulsion-en.svg (not loaded). Dense particle scene: encode {crf: 23} if the file is heavy.

scenes.title: One number for the race

params.curve: schematic: s(x) = s_min + (s_max - s_min) * (1 + tanh((x - rm_c_frac) / width)) / 2 on a 0-1 axis

sentences.text: One number keeps the score: the {param}magnetic Reynolds number{/}, Rm.
It is the {u}flow's speed{/}, times its size, divided by the {param}magnetic diffusivity{/}.
Large Rm: stretching outpaces smudging.
Small Rm: smudging wins.
Turn the Rm knob up, and watch a weak seed field.
At low Rm, the seed dies away.
Past a threshold, the growth rate crosses zero and the seed grows, like the squeal.

scenes.visual: Render class flat. Opens on the two panels of 02.1, which shrink (T1, 1.2 s) into two tokens at the top: a sharp vermillion thread pulled by a blue arrow (tag 'stretching') and a grey-haloed thread (tag 'smudging'). On 'score': the green knob M2 (Kit.knob, label 'Rm', no numbers on its dial) appears left of centre, and the hero equation builds at top centre with Kit.equation (84 px), tex '\term{lhs}{\Rm}\term{eq}{\;=\;}\dfrac{\term{U}{\cu{U}}\,\term{L}{L}}{\term{eta}{\etaP}}': 'lhs' and 'eq' on 'score'. On 'ratio': the terms light in narrative order, U in blue with the label 'flow speed', L in --fg with 'size', then eta in green with 'magnetic diffusivity' (at most two labels at once: the U and L labels fade when eta's appears); the 'stretching' token slides above the fraction bar and the 'smudging' token below it for 1.5 s (leader lines), then both fade. Formula layer item 1. On 'large': the knob turns high (Scene.spring, at most 3 % overshoot); a mini thread glyph beside the knob stays sharp; label 'stretching outpaces smudging'. On 'small': the knob turns low; the glyph blurs; label 'smudging wins'. On 'knob': the knob returns to its minimum; Kit.plot appears on the right (box x 760-1660, y 300-640): x axis 'Rm, magnetic Reynolds number' (param: true, NO numeric ticks: schematic), y axis 's, growth rate' with the zero line in --fg-2; a weak seed field glyph (a short thin vermillion arrow) sits in a small inset above the knob. From 'knob' to 'threshold+2.5' the knob turns slowly up and a point rides the schematic curve s(Rm) (params.curve, s_min, s_max, rm_c_frac, width), drawing it left to right; soft detent ticks (page events, params.knob_detents over the travel). On 'dies': the curve is below zero; the band under the zero line is labelled 'seed dies' and the seed arrow in the inset fades. On 'threshold': where the curve crosses zero, a green dashed vertical line and the label 'threshold Rm_c'; the band above zero is labelled 'seed grows'; in the inset the seed arrow grows (exponential in scene time, then held); squeal callback: the small speaker glyph of 01.3 flashes once beside the inset (no squeal sound). Formula layer item 2. Chip SCHEMATIC on the plot (the curve is a shape, not data; one threshold only here, the windows of 03.4 come later). Badge CONTEXT. Key colours: green, blue, vermillion (three). The growth rate is s (symbol sheet D1), never lambda.

scenes.title: The sodium problem

sentences.text: Laboratory dynamos use liquid sodium.
It flows as easily as water.
But a field smudges in it about a hundred thousand times faster than its swirls do.
Their ratio, one in a hundred thousand, is the {param}magnetic Prandtl number{/}, Pm.
Reaching an Rm of a few tens takes violent stirring.
The flow's {param}Reynolds number{/}, the gauge of turbulence, reaches millions.
So every laboratory dynamo is turbulent.

labels: field smudges about 100 000 × faster than swirls
chips: REFERENCE · Nore et al. 2018 · sodium at 120 °C

scenes.visual: Render class flat. On 'sodium': a grey tank of liquid metal in cutaway (matter grey --matter, a silvery surface line), label 'liquid sodium' (no temperature on the tank: params.sodium_temperature_C = 120 °C is the VKS working temperature of Nore et al. 2018, not that of every experiment, Riga first ran at 205 °C, so it appears only on the formula layer). On 'pm': the green ratio params.pm_label appears between the blobs, nu under the blue swirl with the words 'swirl smudging' and eta under the vermillion blob with 'field smudging'; the reference lower-third 'Reference' / 'Nore et al. 2018 · sodium at 120 °C' for 4 s; formula layer item 2. On 'stir': the blobs slide away; two round dials side by side (about 300 px each), BOTH GREEN because both are control parameters in the colour key (the outline said 'Re blue'; the flow itself is the blue texture): left 'Rm' on a linear dial params.rm_dial with the window params.rm_window shaded green at 12 %; right 'Re, Reynolds number' on a log dial with ticks 10³ to 10⁷ (params.re_dial_log10). On 're': the word 'millions' under the Re dial; formula layer item 3. On 'turbulent': the caption 'Rm ~ 10–50 needs Re ~ millions' at top centre and, under it, 'every laboratory dynamo is turbulent'; the texture at full strength to the end. scenes.title: Three tanks that worked

cards.name: RIGA
cards.line: corkscrew flow → a field that oscillates and turns

cards.name: KARLSRUHE
cards.line: 52 spiralling cells → a steady, dipole-like field

cards.name: VKS
cards.line: two counter-rotating impellers · 150 L of sodium · up to 300 kW → a dipole that can flip

sentences.text: Only three liquid-sodium experiments have made their own field, each a different kind.
In Riga, a corkscrew flow made a field that oscillates and slowly turns.
In Karlsruhe, fifty-two spiralling cells made a steady field, close to a {b}dipole{/}.
And only VKS, at Cadarache, made a dipole that can flip.
A fourth, DRESDYN in Dresden, aims to join them: a spinning cylinder whose axis slowly turns.

labels: corkscrew flow → a field that oscillates and turns
52 spiralling cells → a steady, dipole-like field
two counter-rotating impellers · 150 L of sodium · up to 300 kW → a dipole that can flip

scenes.title: VKS: two impellers and an iron surprise

sentences.text: Inside VKS: a cylinder holding a hundred and fifty litres of liquid sodium.
At its ends, two bladed discs, the impellers, spin in opposite directions.
Should it matter what metal the discs are made of?
With stainless steel discs, there was no dynamo, even at full speed.
Swap in discs of soft iron, and a dipole grows along the axis.
So the threshold depends on more than Rm: materials count too.

labels: two impellers, counter-rotating · motors up to 300 kW
chips: SCHEMATIC · geometry after Monchaux et al. 2007
REFERENCE · Monchaux et al. 2007 · soft-iron impellers

scenes.visual: Render class webgl (Three.js r160 vendored, Line2 fat lines 2-4 px for field lines, matte materials, long lens about 30 degrees, slow orbit of params.orbit_deg over the whole scene, at most 15 degrees per second). On 'discs': two impeller discs with params.blades = 8 curved blades each, near the two ends, spin in opposite directions (one turn per params.disc_turn_s seconds, visual only); label 'two impellers, counter-rotating · motors up to 300 kW'. From 'discs+1.0' the blue flow (--u): short moving blue dashes swirling around the axis in each half, each half turning with its own disc (two cells turning opposite ways), plus the poloidal recirculation loops in the cut plane, drawn as in the site figure figures/vks panel a (same topology and arrow directions). sentences.text: Now spin the two discs at different speeds.
At some settings, the dipole flips again and again, with no schedule.
Like the compass needle at the start, but every minute or two.
Each flip itself takes only about five seconds.
Uneven stripes, like the seafloor's, but written in minutes, not millions of years.

question.en: Simulations cannot reach sodium's *tiny Pm*: which Pm values should the first 3D runs cover?
question.say: Simulations cannot reach sodium's tiny Pm: which Pm values should the first three-dimensional runs cover?
question.fr: Les simulations n'atteignent pas le Pm minuscule du sodium : quelles valeurs de Pm les premières simulations 3D doivent-elles couvrir ?
question.why: Sodium's Pm is about 10⁻⁵, simulations sit near 1, and the Taylor–Green threshold moves from Rm 30 at Pm 1 to 226 at Pm 0.3.
question.unblocks: The Pm values of the Taylor–Green campaign (now 0.5, 1, 2), and which Pm is held out to test the threshold.
question.why_fr: Le Pm du sodium vaut environ 10⁻⁵, les simulations restent proches de 1, et le seuil de Taylor–Green passe de Rm = 30 pour Pm = 1 à Rm = 226 pour Pm = 0,3.
question.unblocks_fr: Les valeurs de Pm de la campagne Taylor–Green (aujourd'hui 0,5 ; 1 ; 2) et la valeur de Pm réservée pour tester le seuil.
